text:
marta: Quick sync — we need to finalize scope & launch criteria for the new 'Inference Advisor' (the Optimize toolkit feature that surfaces batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization recommendations + eval-triggered quality alerts). Customers (ACME, FinCorp) pushed for guidance + alerting. Proposed MVP below. Who can own the spec and provide eng estimates? :eyes:

devon: I like this. One ask: separate "recommendations" from "automations" — MVP should only recommend, not auto-apply. Keeps risk low.

liam: +1 to recommend-only for launch. For quantization, we should provide confidence bands and a canary plan (auto-fallback required by FinCorp).

sasha: From infra POV we need clear perf signals and a perf/latency SLA delta per suggestion. Otherwise teams will ignore suggestions.

marta: Proposed MVP (small scope):
1) Per-route batching suggestion engine — shows expected p95 latency change and token cost delta (high/med/low).
2) Prefix/KV cache recommendation rules — detect cacheable patterns, suggest TTL and cache key.
3) Quantization recommendation UI — list candidate quant profiles with estimated CPU/GPU throughput & expected quality delta. No automatic conversion.
4) Eval-triggered alerts — connect to existing evals: baseline metric + threshold. When drift exceeds threshold, create a ticket + notify route owners.

jordan_cs: Customers want two launch criteria: (A) clear decision docs for ACME/FinCorp workflows; (B) ability to mute/ack alerts for a route. Both are blockers for enterprise customers.

devon: Agree on mute/ack. Also need a minimal rollout plan: start with internal routes (dev-team), then opt-in beta customers, then general availability. Rollout telemetry must include action taken after suggestion.

liam: Engineering questions for estimates:
- Data pipeline to surface per-route token shape and sequences (how long to backfill?)
- Eval integration: hooking alert rules into eval infra (is there an API?)
- Cost model for quant profiles (how to estimate GPU/CPU delta reliably)

sasha: Quick answers:
- We can bootstrap with 7d rolling window of request logs, that'll cover most customers.
- Eval API exists but needs a small adapter.
- Cost model: we already have baseline perf benchmarks for our curated models, we can extrapolate per-seq-length with a conservative multiplier.

marta: Launch criteria proposal (must pass all):
- Feature: Recommendations UI + CSV export + per-suggestion explanation (why this, expected impact).
- Reliability: Suggestions available for 90% of routes in beta orgs (based on 7d data).
- Security: No automated model changes; audit log for every suggestion & alert.
- Enterprise: mute/ack for alerts + canary rollback doc.
- Observability: track suggestion -> action conversion rate and alert false-positive rate.

jordan_cs: For ACME we also need KMS/HSM compatibility on any artifact links. Add that as enterprise acceptance.

devon: Timeline idea: spec by Mar 28 (2w), eng spike + prototype Apr, beta May, GA end of Jun. Is that still end of Q2?

marta: That aligns with target. Need owners: spec owner = marta (I'll write draft), eng lead = liam, ml/research = sasha, CS acceptance = jordan_cs. Can liam give rough estimate next week?

liam: I'll do a 5-point rough estimate after a short spike. Expect 2 x 2-week sprints for core recommenders + 1 sprint for eval integration, then a beta iteration.

sasha: Note: we should include a small opt-in dataset of prompts for regression checks. That will feed eval-triggered alerts. I'll surface the initial prompt set.

marta: Nice. Action items: @liam estimate by 1793600000, @marta spec draft by Mar 28, @sasha prompt set by Apr 7, @jordan_cs list enterprise acceptance details. I'll post a doc link shortly: https://redwood.internal/docs/inference-advisor (draft). :thumbsup:
